mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.5% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based acceleration in economic activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.5% and HOUST > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST rise by at least 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate above 5% without accompanying economic slowdown (as indicated by PAYEMS not falling) signals a hawkish but resilient policy stance, which initially boosts financial sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% in one month AND PAYEMS does not decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive under the specified trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit forecasts, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a rapid labor market deterioration, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls > 1% MoM AND UNRATE rises MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS falls by more than 1% and UNRATE rises in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals broad-based supply-side weakness, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
